selection: one md5-stable parcel for every exact two-signal combination
deidentification: Direct parcel, owner, address, neighbor, prior-owner, corporate, and applicant identifiers replaced with realistic stable aliases; ownership relationships and decision-relevant entity types, numeric facts, and source evidence retained.

cases.review: A one-lot land-development record 236m away is weak parcel evidence. Six differently owned residential neighbors without delinquency do not establish an assemblage strategy.
The sale is real but looks like an ordinary individual residential purchase. The nearby one-lot plan has no shown relationship to the parcel.

The plan title matches the parcel owner, proposes four lots/three units over 45.5 acres, and is only 74m away. The low-value no-structure component is consistent with the plan but approval is not shown.

evidence.project_name: S George St ov Trib to SB

cases.review: The nearby record has zero lots and a different plan identity. Commercial Shopping versus mixed commercial/industrial future use is not a strong parcel-level mismatch without plan authority or timing.
The 101-acre, $1.16m transfer is material. Ten differently owned neighbors create scale context, but no distress or coordinated buyer evidence supports an active assemblage claim.

cases.review: A sub-acre water-company parcel can legitimately lack a mapped structure and assessment. Seven ordinary residential neighbors do not make it an assemblage opportunity.
